name: Wang Junjin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023-2025); Forbes annual (2016-2023); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun China (2006-2026)
forbes_bio: Wang Junjin chairs Juneyao Group, which controls Shanghai-listed Juneyao Airlines.
Wang Junjin co-foundered Juneyao Airlines with brothers Wang Junhao and Wang Junyao; the latter died in 2004.
Wang Junjin holds an EMBA from Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business.

name: Mustafa Kucuk
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Mustafa Kucuk is the biggest shareholder of LC Waikiki, a producer and retailer of ready-to-wear fashions and home items.
Designer Georges Amouyal and a partner founded LC Waikiki in France in 1985. Kucuk and partners including Sefik Yilmaz Dizdar acquired it in 1997.
LC Waikiki's first international store opened in Romania in 2009. In 2016, it expanded into home textile products under the brand name LCW Home.
The company prides itself on promoting women into its management ranks.
Today, LC Waikiki has over 1,000 locations in 47 countries; roughly half are outside of Turkey. Its motto: "Everyone deserves to dress well."
forbes_facts: The brand combines the name of the famous Hawaiian beach with "LC," as in "Les Copains" ("friends" in French).
Mustafa Kucuk avoids the media. His older brother, Vahap Kucuk, is the public face of the company, which pulls in revenue of around $2.5 billion annually.

name: Jitendra Virwani
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun India (2018-2022)
forbes_bio: Property baron Jitendra Virwani's Embassy Group has a mixed portfolio of more than 62 million square feet developed across the country.
Embassy, together with private equity firm Blackstone, listed India's first-ever REIT in 2019.
Embassy has a roster of multinational tenants such as Google, IBM and Warburg Pincus.
In March 2025, Virwani was appointed chairman of listed realty player, Embassy Developments, while his son Aditya was named managing director.
In 2021, Virwani and Warburg Pincus sold their jointly owned Embassy Industrial Parks to Blackstone for $718 million.
forbes_facts: Son Karan oversees a  joint venture in shared office spaces with WeWork. His son Aditya is Embassy's chief operating officer.
Passionate about horses, Virwani owns a riding school in Bangalore.
He has a majority stake in the Indian franchisee of Hard Rock Cafe.
He announced in November 2024 that he is looking to build 150 hotels across India over the next decade.
In March 2025, Virwani was appointed chairman of listed realty player, Embassy Developments, while his son Aditya was named managing director.

name: Zhou Hongyi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2005-2026)
forbes_bio: Zhou Hongyi is the cofounder, CEO and chairman of Beijing-based Internet security software provider and search company 360 Security Technology, also known as Qihoo 360.
Zhou previously founded 3721.com, an online search company that was purchased by Yahoo.
Qihoo delisted from the New York Stock Exchange in 2016 then relisted in China in 2018.
Zhou also chairs Nasdaq-listed 360 DigiTech, a credit information service.

name: Helene Odfjell
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Helene Odfjell is the largest shareholder of Odfjell Drilling, Norway's leading drilling and oil-services group.
The business was founded by her father Abraham Odfjell in 1973 during the early years of the country's oil boom.

She and her sister Marianne inherited Odfjell Drilling, while their brother Johan Odvar Odfjell took over the family's shipping operations in Jo Tankers. In 2015, Marianne exited the drilling company.
Helene Odfjell has been based in the U.K. for decades but relocated to Lugano, Switzerland in 2025.
She is a graduate of the Norwegian School of Economics (NHH) with an MBA from London Business School.
forbes_facts: The Odfjell fortune dates back to 1917, beginning with timber and dry-cargo transport before expanding into chemical tankers.

name: Raj Kumar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Raj Kumar is among Singapore's leading landlords with his Royal Holdings/RB Capital property empire, owned and run together with his son Kishin RK.
After a 2011 family settlement between him and his younger sibling Asok Kumar Hiranandani, also a billionaire, he has been on a deal-making spree.
Prize holdings include the 442-room Holiday Inn Express at Clarke Quay, Holiday Inn Little India and the hotel Intercontinental Singapore Robertson Quay.
He bought the Porcelain Hotel in Singapore's Chinatown, which was refurbished and reopened in 2023 as the 134-room Hotel 1900.
In 2025, they set up their RB Family Office in Abu Dhabi to tap investment opportunities in the Middle East.
forbes_facts: The name RB is derived from the erstwhile Royal Brothers, a 77-year-old property group with roots in textile trading.
Son Kishin's RB Food Group owns a portfolio of brands, such as members' club 1880, cocktail bar Employees Only, Roia restaurant and cloud kitchen company TiffinLabs.

name: Kirill Minovalov
forbes_bio: Kirill Minovalov is the founder of Bank Avangard, which he founded in 1994 with $400,000, a third of which he borrowed.
Bank Avangard grew following the 1998 Russian financial crisis; it now holds assets of about $1.5 billion.
Minovalov also started and now chairs Avangard-Agro, one of Russia's largest and most efficient agricultural manufacturers.
He also owns Avangard Malz, a leading malting company in Germany.
forbes_facts: Minovalov founded a consulting company when he was a student in university.
Avangard-Agro's assets include more than 450,000 hectares of agricultural land in Russia.

name: Cheung Yan
forbes_bio: Cheung Yan chairs Hong Kong-listed Nine Dragons Paper, one of Asia's largest packaging and paper producers.
Cheung's husband Liu Ming Chung, the CEO of Nine Dragons, is also a billionaire.
Cheung's younger brother Zhang Cheng Fei, the deputy CEO of Nine Dragons, is a billionaire, too -- one of three in the family.
Cheung is vice chairman of the Guangdong Federation of Industry and Commerce.

name: Matt Stone
forbes_bio: Matt Stone and his creative partner Trey Parker debuted the foul-mouthed cartoon comedy "South Park" in 1997, writing, producing and voicing more than 300 episodes and counting.

In 2007, Parker and Stone struck a deal with Comedy Central to split the then-non-existent digital revenues for their show 50-50 "in perpetuity," minting them a fortune as streaming revolutionized the TV landscape.
They are also the co-creators of the hit musical "The Book of Mormon," which has been performed on Broadway more than 5,000 times since 2011 and toured around the world.
In July 2025, the pair renewed their deal with Paramount Skydance to create new episodes of "South Park" and payout their half of the digital revenues for an estimated $250 million per year.

name: Yoni Nahmad
forbes_bio: Yoni Nahmad is one of three sons of the late art billionaire Ezra Nahmad, who died in 2023.
Ezra Nahmad, along with his billionaire brother David, was an international megadealer of modern and impressionist art.
At the time of his death, the brothers' art inventory, which is stored in a duty-free warehouse in Geneva, Switzerland, was worth almost $7 billion.
Ezra's half of the collection - which includes works by more than 30 blue chip artists, from Monet and Matisse to Renoir and Rothko - was split evenly among his three sons after his death.
The family also owns 300 Picassos worth at least $1 billion and real estate in London, Monaco and the U.S.

name: Junro Ito
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Junro Ito is the executive chair of Seven & I Holding and the son of the company's late honorary chairman Masatoshi Ito.
Masatoshi Ito, who helped build 7-Eleven into a global giant, died in March 2023 at age 98.
The company is best known for its thousands of 7-Eleven convenience stores in Japan, the U.S. and China. Seven & i Holdings has 87,000 stores in 19 countries.
In 2024, Canadian retail giant, Alimentation Couche-Tard made a $47 billion takeover bid for the company but withdrew in July 2025 citing the retailer's lack of cooperation during negotiations.
Junro Ito joined the company in 1990 and holds a minority stake. His two siblings are also billionaires.
forbes_facts: The company also owns Denny's restaurants in Japan, supermarkets, and financial services firms.
Ito and his siblings were mulling making a $58 billion management buyout of the company but backed out in February 2025 citing financial issues.
In March 2025, the company announced a massive share buyback plan in a bid to bolster the share price.
In March 2025, Seven & I agreed to sell its York Holdings unit which includes major supermarket chains and specialty retailers, to Bain Capital for $5.4 billion.

name: Yang Qiumei
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun China (2024-2026); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Yang Qiumei's wealth derives from a stake in Chinese AI giant SenseTime.
She inherited the stake from her late husband Tang Xiao'ou, cofounder of the company who died in 2023 at age 55.
Yang is a managing director and advisor to the CEO at Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing. She doesn't hold any position at SenseTime.
Prior to joining the Hong Kong bourse, Yang had stints at Investment Company Institute, an industry association of investment funds, and the China Securities Regulatory Commission.
Yang donated in December 2025 $2.6 million to four universities in Hong Kong through her Sophie and Sean Foundation, which was set up in the same year to support innovation and research in AI.

name: Yuan Kokuei
forbes_bio: Kokuei Yuan is a director of Hong Kong-based crypto exchange Bullish.
Bullish was founded in 2020 and went public on the New York Stock Exchange in August 2025.
Yuan owns a 25% stake in the company. Bullish cofounder Brendan Blumer owns 28% and is also a billionaire.
Yuan previously served as executive chairman of block.one, a digital asset investment firm that Blumer cofounded in 2016. Bullish was majority-owned by block.one until 2024.
Yuan, who studied economics and studio art at Tufts University, worked as an investment banker earlier in his career.
